title: Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 7 – Climate Science
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 7, organised by its four Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
course: NSW Earth and Environmental Science Stage 6
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How & why does climate change naturally?

questions.prompt: What natural process warms Earth because atmospheric gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation?
What long-term tectonic cycle can change continent positions and global climate?
What large igneous province in India formed through massive volcanic eruptions near the end of the Cretaceous?
What large igneous province in Russia formed through enormous eruptions near the end of the Permian?
What collective term describes cyclic changes in Earth’s orbit, tilt and precession?
What movement of seawater redistributes heat and can drive natural climate variation?

categories.name: What evidence shows past climate variation?

questions.prompt: What plant remains preserved in sediments can indicate past vegetation and climate?
What frozen cores preserve trapped ancient air bubbles?
What tree-ring dating method can reveal past growing conditions?
What tiny preserved organisms in sediments can provide evidence of past environments?
What cave deposits can preserve isotope evidence of past climate?
What ratios measured in ice, rocks, corals or sediments can act as climate proxies?

categories.name: Has human activity changed climate since industrialisation?

questions.prompt: What gas released heavily by fossil-fuel combustion is a major anthropogenic greenhouse gas?
What term describes the human-caused strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect?
What major historical period saw rapid expansion of fossil-fuel use and industrial emissions?
What ocean chemistry change occurs as seawater absorbs additional carbon dioxide?
What frozen land masses are losing mass as global temperatures rise?
What happens to global mean sea level as land ice melts and seawater warms?

categories.name: How can humans minimise & respond to warming?

questions.prompt: What term describes actions that reduce the causes of climate change?
What term describes adjusting systems or communities to cope with climate impacts?
Replacing coal-fired electricity with solar or wind is an example of what broad strategy?
Building sea walls to protect vulnerable coastlines is an example of what broad strategy?
What land-use action increases carbon storage by re-establishing forests?
What broad term describes deliberate large-scale intervention in Earth systems to counter climate change?

finalRound.prompt: What term describes reducing greenhouse gas emissions or increasing carbon sinks to limit future climate change?
